items.title: Through every point of the image of a flat finitely presented map there is a locally quasi-finite flat chart
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Given a flat, locally finitely presented morphism f : X -> S and a point s in the image, the lemma produces a commutative triangle with g : S' -> S flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite, with s in the image of g and a map S' -> X over S, i.e. an fppf chart of s that is moreover locally quasi-finite and lands inside X. The retained proof is written out in three moves: the fibre X_s is nonempty, the open-ness-of-CM-locus lemma for flat finite presentation supplies a closed point x of X_s where f is Cohen-Macaulay, and the CM slice lemma then yields Z -> S etale-in-the-slice sense through x; setting S' = Z concludes. Retained author proof at lines 6451-6458.
